newsitem.title: GERMANY: US world's fastest expanding book market, fair told.
newsitem.headline: US world's fastest expanding book market, fair told.

text.p: The United States is now the world's fastest expanding book market while once buoyant Britain has been badly hit by the end of price-fixing, the head of the world's biggest book fair said on Tuesday.
"The USA leads the field at the present time in turnover development," said Roland Ulmer at a press conference to launch the 110-nation Frankfurt fair.
He said turnover had risen 5.3 percent this year over 1995 and he predicted turnover would rise by 24 percent by the end of the century.
German publishers attacked Britain at last year's fair for dropping its price-fixing arrangement for books, saying the move could affect booksellers throughout the European Union.
The Net Book Agreement, as it was known, fell apart when three of Britain's largest publishers pulled out. Shops then launched into an orgy of discounting, mainly on bestsellers.
Ulmer painted a bleak picture of the British publishing industry.
"Despite. or because of the virtual removal of price-fixing, book sales have fallen by 4.5 percent from 1994 to 1995," Ulmer told reporters at the fair.
He said English book prices have risen by an average of 6.7 percent over the past 12 months. "In other words, the lifting of controls on prices has not led to cheaper shop prices."
The international publishing industry is now being dominated by chain book stores which in the United States alone account for 80 percent of turnover, he said.
"The traditional independent bookshops are engaged in a desperate struggle for survival," he added.

China leads the book production tables with 103,000 titles, followed by Britain with 95,000 and Germany with 67,000, Ulmer said. Italy ranked as the fastest growing producer with sales rising eight percent a year.
